title: Go SDK streaming implementation guide: context boundaries, cancel-safe prefetch, and retry scenarios
creator: Maya Patel
description: Implement a canonical Go SDK streaming implementation that clearly separates context/cancellation boundaries from transport-level timeouts, demonstrates cancel-safe prefetch/KV cache behavior, and documents retry semantics for partial streams. Deliverables: API surface design, implementation, unit/integration tests, migration notes, and example snippets for customers.
acceptance_criteria: A stable Stream type with documented semantics for cancellation vs deadline propagation
Prefetch/KV cache operations can be canceled without leaking goroutines or corrupting per-session cache
Retryable transient errors produce resumable streams when possible, with clear guidance in examples
Comprehensive unit tests covering cancellation races, backpressure, and shutdown hooks
Migration guide and two example recipes: graceful client cancellation, resumable prefetch, and timed deadline adaptation
steps: Design API: define Stream interface, Context handling rules, and examples for timeouts vs client-initiated cancel
Prototype: implement adapter that decouples transport read loop from user message channel
Prefetch safety: add prefetch cancellation token that drains incomplete prefetch but preserves KV cache consistency
Retry semantics: implement idempotency markers and resumable checkpoints where model supports continuation tokens
Tests: unit tests for context races, integration against runtime staging with simulated network flakiness
Docs: add examples to Go SDK README and code samples repository
Review: get eng + DX review and ship in runtime-1.20 canary
notes: Motivation: many customers have experienced app-layer hangs when users cancel requests; current SDK patterns blur when to use context.WithTimeout vs per-request deadlines
Observations from previous tickets: several long-running streaming tickets (ENG-99988, ENG-73456) pointed to inconsistent cancellation behavior across adapters

Trade-offs considered: exposing explicit CancelStream method vs relying purely on context cancellation. We opted for context-first UX with a cancelable Close method to support deterministic shutdown in server loops
Kernel scheduling: ensure that runtime's continuous-batching path isn't blocked by long-lived client-side cancellation by adding a short jittered drain window before force-close

implementation_summary: Adapter approach: one readLoop goroutine per connection writes parsed messages into a bounded channel (messageBuffer). The public Stream exposes Recv(ctx) which selects on ctx.Done() and messageBuffer. Prefetch operations use a child context derived from the Stream's request context with their own cancel function; on prefetch cancel the buffer is drained deterministically and any partial KV writes are rolled back or committed atomically. Retries are built on resumable checkpoints (resume_token) provided by the server; when server does not provide a token, the SDK falls back to conservative full-retry semantics and surfaces non-resumable errors to callers.
migration_notes: Existing callers that previously relied on implicit connection close behavior should call Stream.Close() or prefer Recv(ctx) with their own context to ensure deterministic cleanup.
We will include a compatibility shim that logs a single warning for callers that do not handle cancellation within 60s post-release (configurable via env var SDK_WARN_UNCANCELLED).
Document example recipes in README: 'client-side cancel with drainage', 'resumable user reconnection', 'deadline vs timeout example for web servers'.
